newsitem.title: THAILAND: Sumitomo says sees baht settling in current range.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo says sees baht settling in current range.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand's offshore currency controls and the underlying strength the economy should see the baht settle around its current trading range within a month, Sumitomo Bank Ltd said on Wednesday.

The Bank of Thailand on Wednesday allowed the baht to float against other currencies, relaxing a rigid exchange regime which has for years allowed limited trading around a rate determined by the strength of a basket of currencies.

The float caused the baht to lose about 15-20 percent of its value in offshore markets by late afternoon, with the currency dropping to around 29.10 baht per dollar in late trade against 24.90 per dollar at the start of the week.
The currency ranged between 27.00-29.10 during the day.
"I think the rate will settle down within this range," Sumitomo's chief representative officer Kozo Yoneda said on Wednesday.
"I think for the moment there will be some big fluctuation of baht but it will gradually go back to its normal level...I think within a month or maybe shorter, within a couple of weeks," he said.

Bank of Thailand officials told Sumitomo it was aware of all currency positions held by both domestic and overseas banks based in Thailand, would continue to control the offshore baht market, and maintain effective control of speculators, he said.

"The Bank of Thailand is strongly confident it can control foreign speculators and will continue to shut down the domestic market (to overseas speculators) as before, and it has every information about the position of Thai banks including foreign banks here," he said.
The underlying strength of the Thai economy also suggested the current levels for the baht were appropriate, he said.

"Sumitomo Bank...has the perception that the Thai economy is basically healthy except the real estate industry which is basically in a bubble. In the manufacturing sector I don't see any problem with that and our Tokyo people share the same view," he said.
The bank's representatives had been called to a meeting of bankers in Bangkok before the announcement was made early on Wednesday and warned about the impending adjustment, he said.
"Sumitomo Bank is not very surprised. Head office is very, very cool and calm," Yoneda added.
Japan is Thailand's single largest foreign investor. More than half of the $5.2 billion in direct foreign investment in Thailand in 1996 came from Japan.
The Bank of Japan has already indicated its willingness to assist the Bank of Thailand should it be required to do so.
